canonical_text: SLM training decision: fine-tune an existing 0.5B-3B instruct model locally with LoRA or QLoRA on the RTX 3070 (8GB VRAM, 64GB RAM); do not attempt full pretraining from scratch, which is not realistic on this desktop.

SLM first run: start with a curated 10,000-30,000-row supervised fine-tuning dataset plus a separate 100-500-question evaluation set; 5,000 strong examples can outperform hundreds of thousands of mediocre ones.

Smol-SmolTalk (HuggingFaceTB/smol-smoltalk, Apache 2.0) is the recommended first experiment dataset because it is adapted for sub-1B models with shorter chat conversations; start with 10,000-20,000 examples, not the whole set.

SmolTalk (HuggingFaceTB/smoltalk) is the best general-purpose SFT source with about one million synthetic samples; select a balanced ~15,000-example curriculum rather than importing everything, noting its weakness is that synthetic data carries repeated styles and systematic errors.

Databricks Dolly 15K (databricks/databricks-dolly-15k, CC BY-SA 3.0) is a good human-generated simple baseline for proving the workflow but should not be the final dataset; preserve attribution and review the share-alike terms.
OpenAssistant OASST1 (OpenAssistant/oasst1) provides human-written multi-turn conversation trees; extract 5,000-15,000 high-quality English conversation paths as a supplement, not the only dataset.
UltraChat 200K (HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k) is useful but too large for a first run and risks a generic voice; take a carefully filtered 10,000-25,000-row subset rather than the first rows.

Microsoft Orca Math (microsoft/orca-math-word-problems-200k, MIT) is only for mathematical-reasoning experiments; cap it at 2,000-10,000 examples in a mixed curriculum because heavy maths distorts the model toward overexplaining ordinary questions.

FineWeb-Edu (HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu) is continued-pretraining material (documents, not instruction pairs), unsuitable for chat tuning; use only a very small streamed subset (2-100 million tokens) for experiments, never the full corpus.

Recommended first SLM mix totals 22,000-25,000 rows: SmolTalk 8,000, OASST1 4,000, Dolly 3,000, SmolTalk specialised reasoning 3,000, Orca Math 2,000, and 2,000-5,000 own governed consultant examples.
Convert every training source into one internal messages format with system/user/assistant turns plus id, source, licence, quality_score and split fields, rather than mixing datasets blindly.

RTX 3070 capability tiers: comfortable for 135M-1B models with LoRA at 512-2,048 tokens; practical but slower for 1.5B-3B QLoRA with gradient checkpointing; borderline for 7B QLoRA; not sensible for desktop pretraining or full 7B fine-tuning.

Architecture decision for Concept Memory Workbench: the SLM should learn behaviour (intent classification, response structure, fluent transitions, evidence boundaries, judgement labelling, refusal, citation formatting, evidence-to-prose), not become the truth store; facts stay in retrieval and governed memory.

SLM evaluation should measure instruction-following accuracy, correct response mode, citation-format compliance, unsupported-claim rate, judgement-labelling accuracy, report-section completeness, verbosity control and desktop latency, not whether the model knows more.

Counterfactual pivot for SLM training: if a good prompt plus retrieval performs within roughly 5-10% of the fine-tuned model on target behaviours, local fine-tuning is not yet justified; improve prompts, retrieval and dataset collection first.

SLM training scenario weights: base case 60% (15k-30k curated examples clearly improve routing and consultant behaviour), bull 20% (1.5B-3B QLoRA replaces some deterministic report phrasing while staying grounded), bear 15% (generic public data degrades governed behaviour and adds hallucination), black swan 5% (contamination, licence or hidden-PII issues make the model undistributable).
Wikipedia decision: include Wikipedia mainly for continued pretraining, RAG retrieval and generating grounded training examples, not as a direct replacement for instruction-tuning data.

wikimedia/wikipedia provides cleaned articles (Nov 2023 snapshot, ~6.41M English articles, CC BY-SA 3.0 and GFDL) but is stale and strips tables and maths; stream a subset rather than downloading the full corpus.

wikimedia/structured-wikipedia preserves sections, paragraphs, links, references and metadata in Parquet under CC BY-SA 4.0, and is the preferred Wikipedia source for the governed source-library and citation design over the flattened dataset.

HuggingFaceFW/finewiki preserves headings, lists, code blocks, tables and mathematics, making it good for technical continued pretraining, but it is a derived dataset whose extraction method, snapshot date and licences must be inspected before use.

Official Wikimedia dumps give the latest snapshots and full parsing control with revision provenance, but pages-meta-current is roughly 45GB compressed; reserve them for later production refresh and revision-handling workflows, not the first SLM experiment.

Wikipedia usage order for the project: first Structured Wikipedia as a governed RAG source, then Wikipedia passages to generate evidence-bound Q&A examples, then a small subset for continued pretraining, and official dumps only when production refresh and revision handling are needed.

Evidence-bound generation rule for Wikipedia: take a source passage, generate a question, answer using only that passage, verify the answer span or entailment, and reject unsupported examples; never let a model invent answers without checking them against the passage.

Wikipedia provenance rule for the data-intake lane: preserve article revision, section, source URL and licence on every Wikipedia-derived record to satisfy CC BY-SA attribution and share-alike obligations.

Wikipedia will not by itself teach conversation, instruction-following, refusal, judgement labelling, citation formatting or consultant recommendations; a balanced mix is Wikipedia text 20-40%, general instruction data 25-40%, governed examples 20-30%, specialist M365 material 10-25% and safety/refusal examples 5-10%.

SLM dataset key variables, ranked by influence: the behaviour to teach (conversation, reasoning, M365 consulting, report writing, retrieval or tool use), dataset quality, model size (0.5B-3B practical), sequence length (drives memory more than row count), licence and provenance, and keeping training and evaluation examples distinct.

Recommended first-experiment model candidates for the RTX 3070: SmolLM2 360M or 1.7B, Qwen2.5 0.5B or 1.5B, Qwen3 0.6B or 1.7B (subject to stack and licence review), or a similarly sized Phi-family base/instruct model after checking the current model card and licence.

Concrete starter dataset recipe (distinct from the larger 22k-25k mix): 10,000 Smol-SmolTalk examples, 2,000 OASST1 examples, 1,000 Dolly examples, 1,000 custom governed-consultant examples, and 200 held-out evaluation examples.

First-run success is measured by behaviour not knowledge: instruction-following accuracy, correct response mode, citation-format compliance, unsupported-claim rate, judgement-labelling accuracy, report-section completeness, verbosity control and desktop latency, not 'does it know more'.

SLM behaviour-training targets for Concept Memory Workbench: classify user intent, select the right response structure, write fluent transitions, obey evidence boundaries, label judgement, refuse unsupported claims, format citations, and turn retrieved evidence into consultant-style prose, while facts stay in retrieval and governed memory.
FineWeb2 (HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-2, ODC-By 1.0) covers more than 1,000 languages but is still pretraining material rather than an instruction dataset, so it is unsuitable for direct chat tuning.

SLM strategy second-order effect: better behavioural tuning can reduce the amount of deterministic code needed, but removing those controls too early can reintroduce hallucination and governance failures.

SLM critical uncertainties: [DATA] the GPU's exact usable VRAM under the intended Windows/CUDA/training stack is unmeasured; [MODEL] the ideal dataset depends on whether the target is chatbot, report writer, router, memory assistant or general LM; [RIVAL] prompt engineering and few-shot may achieve much of the gain without fine-tuning; [MOTIVATED] risk of treating training as progress rather than measuring user-value improvement.

SLM training conclusion: start with Smol-SmolTalk plus a small number of own governed consultant examples and fine-tune a 0.5B-1.7B model with QLoRA; do not begin with FineWeb, millions of rows or pretraining from scratch. Confidence is High on the overall strategy and Medium-high on the exact mix until the dominant target behaviour is fixed.

Wikipedia key variables: whether the use is training, RAG or evaluation; how much data the RTX 3070 can process practically; whether article structure, tables and citations need preserving; dataset freshness; CC BY-SA attribution and redistribution obligations; and filtering article quality and relevance.

Wikipedia continued-pretraining desktop scale: start with 10-50 million tokens for an initial test and 50-200 million tokens for a serious controlled experiment, using article chunks of 512-1,024 tokens and a 135M-500M model initially; do not begin with all 6.4 million English articles.

Wikipedia first-run article selection: take roughly 5,000 general English, 2,000 computing and technology, 1,000 business and organisational, 1,000 science, and 1,000 history and society articles, then remove redirects, disambiguation pages, very short or list-only pages, table-dominated articles, sensitive biographies and weakly sourced or disputed articles.

Wikipedia first-run transform target: convert the selected articles into either 50,000-100,000 clean text chunks for continued pretraining, or 10,000-20,000 evidence-bound instruction examples; the evidence-bound route is preferred for the governed architecture.

Wikipedia counterfactual pivot: move from RAG-first to training-first only if testing shows retrieval latency or context limits materially prevent the model from completing target tasks, and continued pretraining produces a clear, repeatable improvement on unseen domain evaluations.

Wikipedia conclusion: include Wikipedia using Structured Wikipedia as a governed RAG source, 10,000-20,000 Wikipedia-derived grounded Q&A examples, SmolTalk or Smol-SmolTalk for assistant behaviour, own Concept Memory Workbench examples for governance, and a 0.5B-1.7B LoRA/QLoRA model; do not feed full English Wikipedia into the first training run.
